holdout_status.why_it_matters_here: The candidate's per-fold convex simplex weights are fitted against public-validation TARGETS on 3 folds and applied to the 4th. Fold hygiene (verified clean below) makes that construction internally honest; it does not make the resulting score out-of-sample at the corpus level. The frozen blend component carries this further: scripts/phase2_evaluate.py records blend_fit = "all public validation after fold-held evaluation".

methodology_notes.bypass_variant_added: The pre-existing audit feeds adversarial plays through causal_index, which itself drops tick >= cutoff, so it cannot separate "the feature code ignores the future" from "causal_index filtered it first". Added a variant that injects post-cutoff ticks DIRECTLY into the index dicts for the TabPFN/observable path and the two-head path. Both still bitwise identical, so the t < q.cutoff guards inside sample_history() and observable() hold on their own.
methodology_notes.mtd_needs_no_bypass: slot_model.mtd.index() applies NO cutoff filter at all, so the plain mutation test is already the strong form for MTD and PairMTDModel.
methodology_notes.power_controls_added: The pre-existing audit asserts only invariance. An invariance test passes vacuously if the pipeline ignores history altogether, so every test here is paired with a power control: inserting one observation strictly BELOW the cutoff must CHANGE the output. All power controls fired (mtd 12/12, two_head 4/4, tabpfn 3/3, shared_state 12/12).

risk_surface_finding.consequence: In the released files there are ZERO neighbour ticks at or after a target query's cutoff (0 of 5376 target-neighbour pairs on validation). The organizer's index_history() would reject such a file anyway. So the neighbour-future leak condition never arises naturally on this data.
risk_surface_finding.cutoff_homogeneity: Within every episode of train, validation AND test, all 8 machines share one identical cutoff (spread 0 in 96/96, 96/96 and 192/192 episodes).
risk_surface_finding.how_to_read_the_invariance_results: The mutation tests therefore probe a counterfactual: they inject rows that do not exist in any released file. That is still the right test - it proves the code would stay causal under a broader event stream or a heterogeneous-cutoff release - but it should NOT be read as having caught a live risk. The live neighbour-leak exposure on this data is nil by construction of the files, not only by construction of the code.

row_offset_scan.assessment: The only positional slicing of a tick-ordered list in any candidate component is slot_model/mtd.py `for t in rows[20:-19]` inside the changepoint search. It selects WHICH ticks are candidate changepoints; the statistic itself is built with tick arithmetic (range(t-20,t) and range(t,t+20)) guarded by `if s in h` and a len>=15 minimum per side, so sparse older rows cannot masquerade as 20 adjacent observations. Every lag, decay and window in every component is tick arithmetic: h.get(t-k), q.cutoff-lag, q.cutoff-1-t, q.cutoff-w <= t < q.cutoff.

short_history_semantics.interpretation: short_history machines hold exactly 64 pre-cutoff ticks: the 40 ticks [cutoff-40, cutoff) are all present and consecutive, plus exactly 24 older ticks scattered over a much longer span, only a small fraction of which are tick-adjacent. The dense conditions have history count == span, i.e. fully contiguous with no gaps at all.

P1_cutoff_homogeneity_and_surface.conclusion: Every episode in all three splits gives its 8 machines one identical cutoff, so the released files contain ZERO neighbour ticks at or after a target cutoff. The neighbour-future leak condition never arises naturally on this data, and the organizer's index_history() would reject a file where it did. The mutation tests therefore probe a counterfactual: they prove the code stays causal under a broader event stream, not that a live risk was caught.

P2_changepoint_positional_slice.conclusion: The slice only chooses WHICH ticks are candidate changepoints. The statistic uses tick arithmetic range(t-20,t) / range(t,t+20) guarded by `if s in h` and >=15 present observations per side. For short_history only 1329 of 4800 candidates survive, and all 1329 sit inside the dense recent-40 region, so sparse older rows are never averaged as 20 adjacent observations.

P3_label_reachability.conclusion: Inside slot_model/ the only module that touches conditions.csv, targets.csv or reference.csv is official_score.py, a scoring module. No feature builder (features.py, phase2_features.py, phase2_tables.py, mtd.py, mtd_pairs.py, shared_state.py) can reach a condition or target label. In the component scripts they are read only after write_submission, feeding contest_score.

unresolved: Causality establishes only that no component reads a disallowed tick. It is not evidence that the candidate generalises; the 32.260531/60 remains fitted on repeatedly-inspected public validation and is not an independent estimate.

The mutation tests cover the inference path end to end. The TRAINING-time paths were read and reasoned about rather than mutation-tested: MTDModel.fit computes its Dirichlet strength from the unfiltered index (slot_model/mtd.py `props`), which is safe only because the organizer loader guarantees released histories hold no post-cutoff rows AND because strength is frozen in artifacts/mtd_01/change.json (13.333) and never recomputed at predict time. A mutation test on fit() would close this by construction.

The 7 portable HMM summary columns were checked for post-cutoff invariance, but the committed HMM checkpoints under artifacts/phase2/hmm_models were not re-fitted, so their own fold hygiene is taken from the recorded population keys rather than re-derived.
